meanings.note: Masculine: acteur. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'actress'.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.

meanings.note: Une autre = another (one). Descriptive French adjective meaning 'other'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Also a pronoun. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'other'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à quatorze heures. Je vais déjeuner deux fois.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two. I'm going to have lunch twice.

examples.text: Je te jure, c'est une bombe!

as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.note: for things you can't count; de la (feminine)

for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: Un ensemble. Invariable French adverb meaning 'together'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

meanings.note: est-ce que tu viens? = are you coming?

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.

examples.text: C'est le seul exemplaire en France. Je te jure, c'est une bombe!

meanings.note: Ma fille = my daughter. Feminine noun ('la fille', plural 'les filles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'daughter'.

examples.trans: I want to see my daughter.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le film', plural 'les films') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'film'.

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.
Tu as le film de Kechiche.
Vous tournez un film aux États-Unis?

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'un vieux couple qui fait des braquages.

meanings.en: avoir hâte de + infinitive = can't wait to, to look forward to
meanings.note: No article after 'avoir'. Feminine noun ('la hâte', plural 'les —') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'haste'.
Feminine noun ('la hâte', plural 'les —') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'haste'.

examples.trans: I can't wait to read it.
I can't wait to see you.

examples.text: J'ai hâte de discuter de mon contrat.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: c'est incroyable! = I can't believe it! / it's amazing!

examples.trans: You came! I can't believe it!

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: jouer un rôle, jouer le frère de...

Jouer au foot, jouer du piano. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to play'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'joué').

examples.text: Il joue le frère de Guillaume.

meanings.note: je te jure / je vous jure = I swear (to you)
Ces couleurs jurent. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to swear'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'juré').

examples.text: Il jure de ne rien dire.
examples.trans: He swears not to say anything.

examples.text: Je te jure, c'est un film magnifique.
examples.trans: I swear, it's a wonderful film.

related.word: je te jure / je vous jure

meanings.note: Adverb: je veux juste. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Adjective. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: I just want to see Mathias.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to read'.

Before the noun: le même lifting. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'same'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
as an adverb: même Andréa = even Andréa

examples.text: Les actrices américaines ont toutes le même lifting.
examples.trans: American actresses all have the same facelift.

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: at the end of a sentence: super, non?

+ infinitive: pour voir. Core French preposition meaning 'for', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
